title: Dashboard friction postmortem + metric remediation plan (Jan 2026)
content:
Summary:

On 2026-01-10 we observed elevated investigation time for a multi-tenant latency regression that manifested as: slow-first-token for small chat requests and noisy alert churn on the token-latency dashboard. The incident was contained by 2026-01-10 18:30 UTC after rolling back a dashboard-derived alert threshold change and applying a short-term metric filter. This doc records a lightweight postmortem focused on the dashboard friction that prolonged diagnosis and a concrete remediation plan for metric hygiene and dashboard ergonomics.

Why this doc exists (context):
- Operators repeatedly hit confusing panels (duplicate signals, inconsistent labels, hard-to-find filters) which slowed triage.
- Several metrics used different time windows/aggregation semantics; operators compared apples-to-oranges across panels.
- Trace anchors were missing from the quick-investigation view so handoffs to SRE required extra log lookups.

Impact (quantified where possible):
- Median time-to-first-action for the incident was ~22 minutes (typical target <10m).
- Alert noise: ~12 alerts fired in 30 minutes from the same root cause cluster (expected 1-2).
- Pager interruptions: 2 engineers paged for the same symptom because dashboards presented overlapping signals without clear ownership metadata.

Timeline (condensed):
- 2026-01-10 14:07 UTC: Initial user report (Support ticket JIRA-OPS-4123).
- 14:12: alerting started on token-latency-quantile panel (threshold tightened as part of experiment earlier that day).
- 14:18: first investigation runbook executed; operator sees diverging panels but can't map to a single trace id.
- 14:40: triage escalated to SRE; Slack thread started (#ops-incident-2026-01-10).
- 15:05: manual KV cache-prefetch toggle performed for a subset of tenants (short-term mitigation).
- 17:20: rolled-back threshold experiment and adjusted dashboard time window alignment.
- 18:28: incident declared resolved for production surface.

Root causes (hypotheses + evidence):
1) Dashboard aggregation mismatch (high confidence)
   - Some panels used p95 over 1m windows while others used p95 over 5m windows; the inconsistency hid the onset pattern.
   - Evidence: panel queries and widget meta show varying rollup functions (see GH-PR-789 comments).
2) Alerting tied to an experimental threshold (medium confidence)
   - Experiment to reduce alert fatigue tightened p95 limit for a handful of tenants; no canary for alarm churn.
3) Trace anchoring missing from operator view (low->medium)
   - Quick-investigate panel lacked a direct trace link for sessions flagged by the latency panel.

What made diagnosis slow (dashboard friction specifics):
- Duplicate signals: two panels surfaced similar latency metrics but with different tenant scoping (global vs sampled) and different labels.
- Poorly labeled cohort filters: operators didn't know which panel was tenant-weighted vs sample-based.
- Inconsistent aggregation windows across widgets and panels.
- Lack of an "investigation start" query that returns the canonical trace/session id for a highlighted bucket.

Metric remediation proposals (short, medium, long):
- Short (next 1 week):
  - Unify labeling convention: every latency/throughput panel must include an annotation line: "aggregation=window|rollup|cohort".
  - Add panel-level tooltip explaining sampling vs tenant-weighting.
  - Add an immediate rewrite for the p95 token-latency panels to use a canonical 1m window for alerting views.
- Medium (1–2 months):
  - Metric contract enforcement: a linting job that checks widget queries for consistent aggregation/window for panels tagged as "investigation".
  - Create a compact "investigation starter" micro-panel that, given a selected time bucket, returns an ordered list of trace ids and top contributing spans (uses trace sampling API).
- Long (quarterly):
  - Dashboard manifest and ownership metadata: enforce "owner", "alerting-responsible", "sampling-mode" fields for each dashboard tile.
  - Plumb trace links into the console so that clicking a latency bar opens the trace in the tracing UI with the filters pre-applied.

Concrete metric definitions to adopt (copyable guardrails):
- token_latency.p95 (investigation) = p95(latency_ms) computed over 1-minute tumbling windows, tenant-weighted by request count, exclude internal-probes; alert if > 350 ms for 3 consecutive 1m buckets.
- token_latency.p50 = p50(latency_ms) over 1m tumbling windows, sample rate 1%.
- kv_cache_warmth = fraction(prefetch_hit) computed hourly, tenant breakdown optional.
- request_fanout_count.mean = mean(fanout_count) per request sampled across tenants (sampling=1%).

Dashboard ergonomics fixes (immediate patch):
- Consolidate the two conflicting latency panels into a single stacked view with explicit cohort legend.
- Add a compact header to the dashboard: "canonical aggregation: p95/1m / sampling: tenant-weighted".
- Annotate every alerting row with the alert JIRA id and the experiment tag that created it (if any).
- Add a one-click "collect traces for window" button (initially a thin client that launches a trace collection job).

Short-term mitigations applied during incident (lessons learned):
- We rolled back the tightened threshold experiment (owner: Product Observability).
- Applied a restrictive query filter to the alerting rule to prevent tenant-noise (owner: SRE oncall).
- Created a Slack shortcut workflow to collect candidate trace ids from the raw request log and post into #ops-incident.

Action items (owner + reasonable due dates):
- Aisha: submit GH-PR to change canonical window for p95 panels to 1m and add header text (due 2026-01-20).
- Marco: implement panel-level tooltip templates and add to top 5 dashboards (due 2026-01-27).
- Li: design and prototype the investigation-starter micro-panel using trace-sample API (demo 2026-02-10).
- Samir: add lint job to check aggregation/window consistency in dashboard manifests (spike due 2026-02-05).
- Team: run a dashboard review session (owners + product-observability) on 2026-01-25 to sign off on labeling conventions.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do we want investigation panels to all use tenant-weighting or sampling? Pros/cons for cost and operator clarity. (Punted to review session).
- Should we add alerting canaries that measure "alert-churn impact" before rolling threshold experiments?
- How to surface experiment metadata into alert context automatically? (Jira link + tag injection?)

References and artifacts:
- JIRA-OPS-4123: initial user report + support notes.
- GH-PR-789: dashboard query diffs (contains specific query changes that introduced inconsistent rollups).
- Slack thread: #ops-incident-2026-01-10 (investigation chatter and ad-hoc mitigations).
- Confluence guidance (placeholder): /confluence/ops/dashboard-guidelines (to be updated post remediation).

Notes to self / rough checklist while iterating:
- Keep fixes tiny and staged: change header + tooltips first, then rewrite queries, then add lint.
- Make sure owners are accountable for alerts (not just dashboards).
- Document the canonical query examples and paste them into GH-PRs.

Appendix: quick canonical query template (copy into PR)
- SELECT quantile(0.95)(latency_ms) AS p95, tenant_id FROM requests WHERE is_internal = 0 AND timestamp >= $__from AND timestamp <= $__to GROUP BY tumbling_window(1m), tenant_id

If you take one thing from this: add the canonical aggregation header to the dashboard tiles now. It removes confusion rapidly and buys time for the medium-term automation work.

-- Aisha

(keeping this lightweight; if reviewers want a formal 4-part postmortem we can expand with timeline artifacts and exact query diffs)
